metadata.title: The former companion of the hyper-velocity star S5-HVS1

evidence.quote: The hyper-velocity star S5-HVS1, ejected 5 Myr ago from the Galactic Center at 1800 km/s, was most likely produced by tidal break-up of a tight binary by the supermassive black hole SgrA*.
Koposov et al. (2020) reported a hyper-velocity star (HVS) S5-HVS1 that is confidently associated with the Galactic Center (GC).

The most likely mechanism is the tidal break-up of a tight binary system by the supermassive black hole (BH) SgrA* (Hills 1988), where one star is ejected to infinity at high speed and the other is bound.

notes: S5-HVS1 is classified as follow_up because the paper cites Koposov et al. (2020) for the prior HVS identification and adopts the Hills-breakup interpretation with one component ejected to infinity (T:p1-b12). No Gaia identifier is supplied for S5-HVS1.

S5-HVS1: The target star S5-HVS1 is discussed only as the ejected member of the binary. The paper reports for S5-HVS1 its approximate mass (~2.3 M_sun; adopted m_e = 2.35 M_sun in Fig. 3/Fig. 4), its inferred ejection speed from the Galactic Center (~1800 km/s), its age (30–100 Myr), and metallicity ([Fe/H] ~ 0.3). None of these correspond to the eligible quantity identifiers (mass, ejection speed from the GC, age, and metallicity are not among ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motions, heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probability). No equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for S5-HVS1. All other quantitative results in the paper (Table 1 survival probabilities, Table 2 orbital properties, pericenter/a estimates, etc.) refer to the captured former companion, not to S5-HVS1, so they are not extracted here. No eligible quantities for S5-HVS1 are therefore available.
